description: Phase 10 play-segmentation benchmark: manual timestamp pass-through, automatic snap detection from collective motion onset, automatic play-end detection from motion cessation, per-frame phase labelling (pre_snap / snap / play / play_end / snap_unknown), evidence accounting, and refusal behaviour across frozen TRAIN / VAL / TEST splits.

benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.player_motion: Synthetic deterministic field-space speed profiles (rectangular onset/cessation, staggered ramps, partial-group motion, pre-snap movers). Timings and speeds are engineering fixtures, NOT recorded NFL player trajectories.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.trajectories: FieldTrajectory / TrajectorySample objects constructed directly in field space. They are NOT the output of the Phase 1-4 image pipeline on video: no frames are decoded, no homography is fitted, no detector runs. Phase 10 is measured as a consumer of Phase 4 contracts.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.ground_truth: Snap and play-end frames are properties of the fixture construction (the frame the first mover crosses the speed threshold, the frame motion stops). There is no whistle audio, no referee signal, no independently annotated broadcast clip and no real play clock.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.geometry: Each sequence carries one synthetic coordinate_frame_id ('synthetic:<sequence_id>') except the explicit camera-cut sequence, which switches to a second synthetic frame. No absolute yard line is claimed anywhere; x_coord_mode is 'relative_10yd' by construction.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.image_detector_accuracy: UNMEASURED. Phase 10 never sees an image. Nothing in this benchmark is evidence that image-based player detection, tracking or projection is solved.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.end_to_end_video_accuracy: UNMEASURED. The unattended video runner (football_vision/evaluation/video.py) does not segment plays, because a play START is always a manual timestamp in this design; no video-to-play-segmentation accuracy exists.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.team_labels: Not used. Segmentation is team-agnostic; collective motion does not require offense/defense identity.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.thresholds: All thresholds are the frozen a priori defaults in football_vision/analytics/segmentation.py (motion speed 1.0 yd/s, onset fraction 0.45, baseline fraction 0.15, baseline 10 frames, sustained 3 frames, min tracks 6, quiet 6 frames, min play 6 frames). They were not fitted on any split, and TEST was not used to select them.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.expectations: Each play declares a frozen 'expected' block (maximum tolerated snap/end error in frames, or the refusal reason that must be produced). Expectations are pass criteria declared before running; 'expectation_violations' counts mismatches and must be 0. An expectation is not a claim that the behaviour is good for real football.
benchmark_provenance_and_semantics.refusal_semantics: A refusal is 'false' when the fixture ground truth contains a snap (or play end) that the segmenter did not emit, and 'true' when the fixture declares no determinable boundary. False refusals are reported, never hidden: they are the documented cost of a refusal-first design on low-visibility strata.

splits.TRAIN: Development inspection split: clean onset, a pre-snap mover, and a too-few-visible-tracks stratum.
splits.VAL: Threshold-sensitivity strata: staggered (gradual) onset, partial-group motion below the onset fraction, and a mid-play camera cut.
splits.TEST: Frozen held-out split: baseline evidence gaps from occlusion, a two-play drive with mixed manual/automatic boundaries, a never-quiescent window, and a dead-reckoning-only window. Nothing was tuned on it.

sequences.description: Clean 22-player window: 20 quiescent frames, collective motion from frame 20 to 59, quiescent again to 79. Manual label supplies only start_frame; snap and play end must both be recovered automatically.
One backfield player goes in motion at frames 8-17 before the snap at frame 25. Pre-snap motion must not be mistaken for the snap: 1/22 = 0.045 stays under the 0.15 baseline fraction.

Broadcast close-up stratum: only 4 tracks are visible, below min_tracks=6, so the moving fraction is not statistically meaningful and the snap must be refused even though a play exists. The play end is a manual timestamp and must pass through unchanged.

Staggered onset: the 22 players cross the motion threshold over 6 frames starting at frame 30 (a real snap is not instantaneous in field space), and the play end is left to motion cessation. The detector reports the first frame of the sustained collective run, so a small positive latency is expected and bounded, not hidden.

Pile / heavy-occlusion stratum: a play exists at frame 25 but only 35% of the visible group ever produces reliable measured motion, so the 0.45 onset fraction is never reached. Correct behaviour is a refusal (false refusal against ground truth), not a guess.

Camera cut at frame 40 changes the coordinate frame mid-play (snap 20, end 60). Speeds are not comparable across coordinate frames, so the whole window must be refused with coordinate_frame_change rather than segmented anyway.

Occlusion stratum on a small visible group: 4 of 8 tracks coast (dead reckoning) during frames 5-9, so those frames have fewer than min_tracks usable measured samples. An undefined frame is unknown motion, not a quiet frame, so the pre-snap baseline cannot be established.

Two-play drive. Play 1 is fully manual (start/snap/end pass-through, never recomputed). Play 2 supplies only a manual start frame, so both its snap and its dead-ball frame must be recovered automatically. Verifies ordering, non-overlap and mixed manual/automatic provenance inside one result.

Warm-up / celebration window: the visible group is already moving at the manual start frame and never becomes quiescent, so there is no pre-snap baseline and no snap exists. The correct result is a true refusal and snap_unknown phase labels.

Total-occlusion stratum: every sample in the window is a coasting dead-reckoning prediction (no accepted measurement anywhere). Dead reckoning is model output, so no collective motion may be inferred and no boundary may be claimed.
